# Wasabi Drive Backend — GitHub Copilot Repository Instructions

These instructions apply to **GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code (VS Code)** when working inside the **backend repository** `api-wasabi-drive`. The owner implements on a **personal Windows laptop**; it can reach Wasabi, but technical connectivity **never** constitutes approval for live access. Treat this file as repository-wide guidance; execute only the explicitly requested task. Do not use an external coding-agent or cloud-hosted workspace as a substitute for the approved local workflow.

## Ownership, branch discipline, and permission boundaries

- The human developer is the technical owner and approves architecture, provisioning, operational access, rollout, and deployment. AI assists with narrowly scoped implementation and independent review; it does not make those decisions.
- Use the current checkout as authoritative, inspect `git status`, current branch/SHA and relevant tests before editing. Create/use the approved focused branch `feature/thumbnail-access-url-pilot` only when this task prompt is invoked for implementation; never commit directly to protected `master`.
- Do not commit, push, open a PR, merge, provision resources, change access policies/credentials, access real Wasabi objects, or deploy without separate explicit authorization for that action. Leave code changes uncommitted for owner review. Never overwrite uncommitted owner work.
- Preserve the working deployment and tests. Do not perform unrelated refactors, dependency upgrades, formatting sweeps, `npm audit fix`, or speculative infrastructure work.

## Copilot working agreement for VS Code on Windows

- Use **Copilot Chat's local Agent/editing workflow** for this focused task; inspect current files and propose the smallest patch, then edit and run only authorized **local mocked** checks. If Copilot can access a terminal, ask for the owner's approval before commands that could contact a real service or change durable state. Never treat an auto-approved tool command as permission to access Wasabi.
- Before editing, report the actual `git branch --show-current`, `git status --short` and `git rev-parse HEAD` results. If on `master` and the tree is clean, the implementation prompt authorizes creating `feature/thumbnail-access-url-pilot`. If the tree is dirty or another task branch has changes, **stop without resetting, stashing, rebasing or force-switching** and report the conflict. Do not invent a SHA from an archive as the current HEAD.
- Allowed for the implementation task: repository source reads, local source edits, focused mock tests, `npm test` on Node.js 24, and `git diff --check` / `git diff --stat` / `git status` inspections. Dependency installation via `npm ci` is permitted only if needed to run local tests and must not modify the lockfile; do not invoke deployment or integration scripts.
- **No live Wasabi calls of any kind** during implementation, even read-only metadata or testing signed URLs. Do not inspect private checkpoint/audit files, local secret stores, `.env` files containing real credentials, or production bucket/object contents. Do not copy private local data into Copilot chat, fixtures, logs, source comments or committed docs.

The owner will explicitly authorize and supervise that validation later, using TEST-only buckets, credentials and fixtures. Never redirect TEST at PRD or bypass the integration harness' restrictions.
- After editing, explain each change and provide actual test evidence. Leave code uncommitted and wait for independent ChatGPT/owner review. No autonomous next-phase work, PRD operations, or frontend changes.

## Existing architecture — preserve it

- Node.js 24, Express 4, CommonJS, AWS Lambda, API Gateway REST API, Serverless Framework v4/CloudFormation, AWS SDK for JavaScript v3, private S3-compatible Wasabi storage, `test`/`prd` stages.
- HTTP route -> application/service -> storage adapter -> Wasabi SDK. Preserve `src/app.js` (Lambda app) versus `src/server.js` (local startup); keep configuration centralized in `src/config/index.js`.
- React/MSAL (Microsoft Authentication Library) obtains Microsoft Entra OAuth 2.0 access tokens. Express authenticates them and the trusted-user middleware authorizes access. Authentication is not authorization; API keys and Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) are neither user authentication nor authorization. Backend checks remain authoritative.
- Existing `AccessUrl` is a signed URL for the **original object** (currently 3,600 seconds). Preserve the field, original storage signing, current pagination, folder listings and error behavior.
- `src/storage/wasabi.js` resolves the **source bucket's** region with a cached lookup. Do not substitute the configured default Wasabi region, the Singapore destination region, or the AWS Lambda deployment region for this source region.
- `src/thumbnail/key.js` (`createThumbnailKey()` / `normalizeEtag()`) defines immutable v1 identity; `src/thumbnail/eligibility.js` provides image-eligibility rules. `src/thumbnail/index.js` stays lightweight. Do not duplicate the hash formula or normalize/trim source object keys.
- Express/module startup must not import Sharp, `extract-raw-preview`, image-processing services, production-backfill/storage-write modules, Docker utilities, or local CLIs.

## Active task: Phase 8C-D1 (backend only)

Add optional `ThumbnailAccessUrl` to `Contents[]` in existing **authorized** object-list responses, solely for exact approved existing derivatives. Preserve `AccessUrl` and every existing response field; omit the new property when disabled, out of scope, missing identity/metadata, not allowlisted, or thumbnail signing fails. Do not make original browsing depend on thumbnail success.

1. **Enrichment and source scope.** Only consider objects from a configured exact source bucket, resolved source region, and nonempty slash-terminated source prefix. Reuse the listing's full `Key`, `ETag`, and metadata. Use `evaluateThumbnailEligibility()` where suitable (derive extension without changing source key). Generate candidate keys via `createThumbnailKey()`, never by reimplementing hashing. Match against an encapsulated, exact-key `Set` of verified derived keys. The allowlist is pilot **coverage**, not user authorization.
2. **No speculative storage requests.** Do not add per-object `HeadObject`, separate per-image region lookups, listing all derivatives, or remotely checking for object existence while browsing. An allowed candidate is enough to sign a URL. Reuse `wasabi.getBucketRegion()` after listing: it already resolves through the same cached region mechanism.
3. **Dedicated read-only signer.** Implement a small, separate signer (suggest `src/storage/thumbnail-api-wasabi.js`) with a fixed backend-configured **derived** bucket, Singapore regional endpoint/region, explicit dedicated derived-read Wasabi access key/secret, and `GetObjectCommand` + `getSignedUrl()` only. Do not use the SDK default credential chain, API `WASABI_*` credentials, TEST backfill credentials, production backfill credentials, or audit credentials as fallbacks. Do not add any write or delete operations. At runtime the derived identity requires `s3:GetObject` only on the approved private derived-object scope; no `s3:PutObject`, `s3:DeleteObject`, or bucket listing permission is needed for presigned GETs.
4. **Independent internal-bucket protection.** Filter **configured internal derived buckets** from `getListBuckets()` without changing other response metadata. Reject normal object-list and bucket-region requests directed to any such bucket **before** storage calls. Use a sanitized consistent HTTP 404 response so an internal bucket is not browsable even when thumbnail URL enrichment is disabled. Keep existing authn/authz middleware preceding all `/buckets` routes. Do not introduce per-user ownership authorization in this task.
5. **Feature flag and validation.** Disabled by default, with no new signing credentials required. When enabled, require explicit stage-specific destination, source scope, read credentials, exact key allowlist, and safe URL lifetime. Reject unknown enablement strings, bad/missing source prefix, invalid region, malformed/wildcard/duplicate keys, unexpected destination or reuse of the original credential identity. Never widen scope on invalid config. The v1 namespace remains fixed by the existing key helper. Preserve an independently configured `WASABI_INTERNAL_BUCKETS` value so internal buckets are hidden even while enrichment is disabled.
6. **Failure boundary.** Original listing/authentication/authorization/original signing failures retain existing behavior. Only optional thumbnail lookup/signing errors degrade gracefully to no `ThumbnailAccessUrl`. Diagnostics may contain a sanitized category and count, but no raw errors, presigned URLs, signature query strings, personal source paths, full keys, ETags, tokens, or credentials.
7. **Do not create an arbitrary derived-object signing endpoint**, proxy bytes through Express, generate images on list requests, modify the transform recipe, change object ACLs, make a bucket public, or introduce extra cloud services.

## Proposed runtime config names (validate against current source before implementation)

- `WASABI_INTERNAL_BUCKETS`: comma-separated exact internal derived bucket names, stage-specific and independent of the thumbnail feature flag. Must include the active derived bucket when enrichment is enabled. Configure for each deployed stage **before merge**. A deployed `test`/`prd` stage without a valid nonempty internal-bucket list must fail configuration validation rather than silently leave the internal bucket visible; local/mock configurations without a deployment stage may remain disabled.
- `THUMBNAIL_API_ENABLED`: absent/`false` means disabled; `true` means enabled; any other supplied value is invalid.
- When enabled: `THUMBNAIL_API_SOURCE_BUCKET`, `THUMBNAIL_API_SOURCE_REGION`, `THUMBNAIL_API_SOURCE_PREFIX` (nonblank and trailing `/`), `THUMBNAIL_API_DERIVED_BUCKET`, `THUMBNAIL_API_DERIVED_REGION`, `THUMBNAIL_API_ALLOWED_KEYS` (comma-separated exact v1 keys), `THUMBNAIL_API_READ_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `THUMBNAIL_API_READ_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `THUMBNAIL_API_URL_TTL_SECONDS` (integer 60–3600; recommended 3600).
- Enforce the existing v1 namespace (`THUMBNAIL_FORMAT_VERSION`) rather than introducing a configurable version that could silently change identity. Allowlist members must match `v1/<2 hex>/<64 hex>.webp`, with the two-character shard matching the digest; no prefix or wildcard coverage. Cap this pilot's allowlist at 13 unique keys. Do not store real keys/personal folder names in source or tests.
- Validate a supported Wasabi region using `src/storage/wasabi-regions.js`. Require source and destination buckets to differ and require the configured source region to match actual resolved region. For this approved pilot, the **destination** is Singapore (`ap-southeast-1`); production source is Tokyo (`ap-northeast-1`). Never silently substitute TEST or PRD destination configuration.
- Inject optional variables through the existing `serverless.yml` and protected TEST/PRD GitHub Environment workflows. Keep private prefix/allowlist/credentials in Environment secrets; do not echo them. Empty optional values must not cause the disabled API to fail boot. Confirm environment-size and Serverless variable-resolution behavior before approving deployment. Never commit real values or policy changes.

## Validation, rollout and rollback boundaries

- For this explicitly requested local implementation, run mocked focused tests and `npm test` under Node.js 24; inspect `git diff --check`, `git diff --stat`, `git status --short`, all untracked files, and any accidental secret-bearing changes. Report actual commands/results; do not reuse historical 285-test totals as fresh evidence.
- `npm run test:integration` is the existing **TEST-only** authenticated Bruno regression; it needs separate authorization and suitable TEST token/fixtures. Never bypass its production restriction. Existing smoke checks are separate.
- Before merging, verify protected GitHub TEST configuration: a dedicated TEST source and private TEST derivatives; no production source or destination in TEST. Merge to `master` **automatically deploys TEST**, so this is a real deployment gate. No deployment without owner approval.
- An end-to-end TEST pass requires a genuine signed private WebP retrieval, working original `AccessUrl`, failed anonymous raw-object access, and absence of thumbnail URLs on unprocessed objects. Presigned URL generation alone is insufficient. Only the owner authorizes live validation.
- PRD enablement requires closure of the independent final-five verification and reconciled 13-key allowlist, an explicitly approved promotion, and backend-before-frontend compatibility. A configuration change alone does not update a deployed Lambda; the approved deployment workflow must apply it.
- Roll back first by disabling thumbnail enrichment and redeploying through the existing controlled workflow. The backend optional field is backward compatible; a later frontend must tolerate missing thumbnails. Retain internal-bucket protection on rollback if possible. Never delete derivatives, edit checkpoint state, or rerun the completed backfill.
- Stop at Phase 8C-D1. Do not implement 8C-D2 frontend changes, measure performance, expand production coverage, revisit SNS/Lambda processing, migrate to Vite/TypeScript, or redesign the UI in this task.
